references.text: God tells Abraham that his descendants will be strangers in a land that is not theirs and will be enslaved there, but that God will judge the nation they serve, and afterward they will come out with great possessions.
God renews the promise to Abraham through Isaac, promising to give these lands to his descendants and to fulfill the oath He swore to Abraham.
God renews the promise to Abraham and Isaac through Jacob, promising him the land he was lying on for himself and his descendants, and that his descendants will be like the dust of the earth.
God speaks to Israel (Jacob) in a night vision and says not to be afraid to go down to Egypt, for He will make him into a great nation there. God also promises to bring him back up from Egypt.
Israel (Jacob) assures Joseph that God will be with them and lead them back to the land of their fathers.
God tells Moses that He has seen the suffering of His people in Egypt and that He will bring them out of Egypt's misery into a land flowing with milk and honey.
When the Lord brings the Israelites into the land of the Canaanites, which He swore to their forefathers to give them, they are to observe this service.

Moses took Joseph's bones with him, for Joseph had made the children of Israel swear, saying: 'God will surely visit you, and then you shall carry my bones away from here.' – a direct fulfillment of Joseph's words.
God commands Joshua to be strong and courageous, for he is to lead this people to inherit the land which God swore to their forefathers to give them.

Stephen recounts that as the time for the fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham drew near, the people grew and became numerous in Egypt – a reference to the fact that God's visitation (paqad) was near.
By faith Joseph, when he was dying, spoke about the Israelites' exodus from Egypt and gave instructions concerning his bones – a direct reference to Gen 50:24-25.
Prophecy and fulfillment: The promise in the source verse to lead the people out (Gen 50) is met here at the beginning of the actual exodus based on the same oath.
Theological basis for the giving of the land: Both verses confirm that the entry into the land rests on God's oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God's own confirmation: Joseph believed in God's promise (Gen 50), and here God Himself confirms that He will complete this promise to give the land to his descendants.
Contrast in leadership: Both Joseph (Gen 50) and Moses (Deut 34) die before the fulfillment, underscoring that the promise to the fathers stands firm regardless of the leader.
Prophetic continuity: Confirms that the promise of inheritance based on the oath to the fathers (mentioned in Gen 50) remains valid much later in history.
Motivation for action: Explains the theological basis in Gen 50 – that the exodus occurs to fulfill God's oath to the fathers, not because of the people's own actions.
